note: The fuzz input length directly controls the allocated buffer size used to build the in-memory file.
The raw input bytes are copied into the heap buffer that is then passed into htslib.
The copied bytes become the backing storage for the memory-backed hFILE consumed by hts_open.

The filename must not be treated as containing the index delimiter unless the delimiter is actually present; otherwise later pointer arithmetic can derive an invalid split point from the input string.
Opening the memory-backed URL with the derived filename path reaches the vulnerable parsing path that can read past the end of the provided bytes.
